content.overview: Unless the articles require a larger number, one-fourth of the total membership shall constitute the quorum at a general meeting of a Producer Company.
content.glance: Default quorum is one-fourth of total membership; articles may require a larger number but may not reduce it below the statutory floor.
content.study: Section 378Y fixes the default quorum for general meetings of a Producer Company at one-fourth of the total membership. The articles may prescribe a larger quorum. Quorum is measured by number of Members, not by share capital.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: Unless the articles require a larger number, one-fourth of the total membership constitutes the quorum at a general meeting.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378Y
examples.body: A Producer Company with 80 Members needs at least 20 Members present for a valid general meeting under the default one-fourth quorum rule.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378Y?
hypotheticals.analysis: It fixes the default general-meeting quorum at one-fourth of total membership, subject to a larger number in the articles.

misconceptions.trap: Measuring quorum by share capital rather than membership.
misconceptions.correction: s. 378Y uses total membership, not share capital.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 378Y be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State the one-fourth default. II. Check whether the articles require a larger number. III. Conclude on quorum.

revisionPoints: Quorum — one-fourth of total membership (articles may require more)
